newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agency seeks $17.5 mln to update, improve CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agency seeks $17.5 mln to update, improve CPI.

text.p: The Labor Department said Thursday it is seeking $17.5 million in the 1998 fiscal year as part of its ongoing effort to update and improve the Consumer Price Index as a measure of the cost of living.

The funding request for the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics includes $15.4 million for a continuing revision of the CPI that began in the 1995 fiscal year that it said will ensure accurate, reliable and timely data.

The bureau is scheduled to begin using its revised index on a new market basket in its January 1998 data, introduce a revised housing sample with the January 1999 data and finish the revision in the fiscal year beginning Oct. 1, 2000.

The other $2.1 million in funding sought for the CPI is for the first year of a multi-year effort that would strengthen the "statistical and methodological infrastructures" of the CPI program, the department said.

The improvements would would make the CPI more responsive to changing conditions, provide alternative measures to cost of living changes, improve its measure of product quality and better reflect the impact of newly introduced goods on the cost of living, it said.
